analysis.investment_thesis: Exato is a tiny newly-listed IT services outfit with good ROE (28%) but a decelerating top line — revenue growth collapsed from 56% (FY24) to just 9% (FY25) — while P/E of 35 bakes in fast-grower expectations. PEG on sustainable growth is materially >1.5, borrowings tripled, and the "story" isn't yet clear enough to warrant the premium.
key_strengths: Strong returns profile: ROE 28.2%, ROCE 26.5% — capital-efficient operator
Net profit doubled FY25 (5→10 Cr) as operating margin expanded to ~11%
Promoter holding healthy at 54.73%, skin-in-the-game intact
key_risks: Revenue growth decelerated sharply 56%→9%; PEG ~4x on top-line — red flag
Borrowings ballooned 6→17→28 Cr; FCF went 10→-20→0 over 3 years
Tiny 338 Cr IT-ITeS micro-cap with no disclosed moat, customer concentration likely
red_flags: Growth deceleration — the classic Lynch 'story weakening' signal
Debt up ~4.7x in two years while operating cash flow is erratic
Recent BSE listing with limited operating history at public-company scale
analysis.detailed_analysis: What's the story here? A 2016-incorporated customer-transformation IT shop that rode one strong year (FY24 revenue +56%) and is now flat-lining at 9% growth in FY25. At 35x earnings, the market is pricing this as a fast grower, but the actual top-line trajectory says stalwart-at-best. My PEG discipline — P/E no more than the growth rate — is violently breached here; even generously annualizing the doubling of net profit, the revenue deceleration tells me FY25 earnings jump is margin-driven and not repeatable. That's exactly the kind of optical "earnings growth" that traps multiples expansion investors.\n\nThe balance sheet compounds my concern: borrowings jumped from 6 Cr to 28 Cr while cumulative 3-year FCF is roughly -10 Cr. They're funding growth with debt, not cash, which in a services business with 28% ROE is a puzzling capital-allocation choice. I like the returns metrics and the promoter holding, but I need to see two more years of 20%+ revenue growth with improving FCF before this becomes a Lynch-style GARP candidate. Pass at 414; revisit if it corrects to a PEG below 1 or revenue re-accelerates meaningfully.
